curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42052-1-1.pdf (one book: finished on page 188; pages 190-191 show the battery box switch, the two selector levers and functions A-D)

functions.does: One Power Functions M-motor, switched on and reversed at the battery box under the nose, drives everything through a gearbox behind the cockpit: its 12-tooth gear turns a 24-tooth gear on the gearbox's right shaft, and a row of 16-tooth gears carries the drive across to the left shaft, so both shafts with driving rings always turn while the motor runs.
functions.source: book: gearbox steps 87-98 (pages 47-52), page 190 (the battery box switch, with a two-way arrow); inferred: the gear path

functions.does: Function A: with the lever on the right side behind the cockpit pushed to A, the motor turns the two coaxial three-blade rotors: the right shaft's driving ring locks its rear 16-tooth clutch gear, which turns through two idler clutch gears and a gear above them to a 16-tooth gear on the rotor drive shaft; its two 12-tooth bevel gears turn the two rotor turntables, one from above and one from below, so the rotors turn opposite ways.
functions.source: book: page 190 (the right lever, positions A and B), page 191 (A: the rotors turning), gearbox steps 87-98 (pages 47-52); inferred: the gear path and that the rotors counter-rotate
functions.note: unsure which way the lever must turn for A (the sign of 'by')

functions.does: Function B: with the right lever pushed to B, the motor lowers or raises the rear loading ramp: the right shaft's driving ring locks its front clutch gear, which turns a 16-tooth gear on a shaft running back through a universal joint to a worm gear; the worm turns an 8-tooth gear whose cross shaft's liftarms swing the ramp on its links.
functions.source: book: page 190 (the right lever, positions A and B), page 191 (B: the ramp swinging down), gearbox steps 87-98 (pages 47-52); inferred: the gear path
functions.note: unsure which way the lever must turn for B (the sign of 'by')

functions.does: Function C: with the lever on the left side pushed to C, the motor swings the two orange side panels (the cargo bay doors) out and in: the left shaft's driving ring locks its rear clutch gear, which turns a 16-tooth gear on a shaft with a worm gear; the worm turns an 8-tooth gear whose cross shaft's liftarms and links swing both doors on their hinges.
functions.source: book: page 190 (the left lever, positions C and D), page 191 (C: the side panels swinging out), gearbox steps 87-98 (pages 47-52); inferred: the gear path
functions.note: unsure which way the lever must turn for C (the sign of 'by')

functions.does: Function D: with the left lever pushed to D, the motor winds the winch, raising or lowering the hook on its string under the fuselage: the left shaft's driving ring locks its front clutch gear, which turns a 16-tooth gear on a shaft whose 20-tooth gear turns a 12-tooth gear on a worm shaft; the worm turns an 8-tooth gear on the winch reel.
functions.source: book: page 190 (the left lever, positions C and D), page 191 (D: the hook going up and down), gearbox steps 87-98 (pages 47-52); inferred: the gear path
functions.note: unsure which way the lever must turn for D (the sign of 'by')

functions.does: With a lever in the middle, between its two positions, its driving ring locks neither clutch gear and neither of its functions runs.
functions.source: inferred: how driving rings work; the book's lever pictures (page 190) show only the end positions

functions.does: The landing gear's wheels roll freely: two small nose wheels and two larger main wheels.

questions.question: Which way does each lever go for which function? The `first` amounts in this file are guesses.
